newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle markets quiet - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle markets quiet - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Monday were at a standstill as light bids at $62.00 per cwt were passed by owners pricing cattle $64.00 to $65.00, feedlot sources said.
The bids were down $1.00 from last week's sales of $63.00, with weakness tied to the lack of aggressive beef business, the sources said.
Cattle owners were holding firm to higher asking prices amid ideas that packers were short-bought and would need to replenish live inventories, they said.
Support in fed cattle prices could be offset by this week's larger showlists following carryover from last week of cattle held back by owners resisting lower prices.
Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma showlist was estimated near 86,500 head, up 5,500 and the Kansas showlist was pegged near 88,500 head, up 10,000, market sources said.

Light beef demand also could weigh on feedlot cattle prices, with possible limited buying as Lent starts on Wednesday, the sources said. Religious dietary guidelines call for meat abstinence by Catholics on Ash Wednesday and all Fridays during Lent until Easter, March 30.
